report.incidentSummary: On 2026-09-18 at approximately 05:35 UTC (11:05 IST), auth-service OTP login success rate dropped sharply from ~97.5% to ~75-78%, causing about a quarter of user logins to fail with reports that entered OTP codes were invalid. Telemetry rules out the reporter's initial suspicion of SMS provider or notification-service delivery failure. The degradation was triggered by planned cache maintenance CHG-48222 (cache primary failover at 05:32 UTC), which introduced replica desynchronization or split routing for OTP verification state.
report.rootCauseStatement: Planned infrastructure maintenance CHG-48222 executed a cache primary failover at 05:32 UTC, resulting in state desynchronization or split routing between auth-service instances and cache replicas. Active OTP tokens generated across nodes resulted in code mismatch verification failures for ~25% of attempts.

hypotheses.cause: Planned cache primary failover (CHG-48222) at 05:32 UTC caused cache state desynchronization, replica lag, or split routing between auth-service instances and cache nodes, leading to code mismatch verification failures.
hypotheses.rationale: CHG-48222 completed at 05:32 UTC, exactly 3 minutes prior to the onset of OTP login failures at 05:35 UTC. Auth-service has a critical downstream dependency on cache. Verification errors specifically report code mismatches rather than missing keys, and historical incident PIR-1670 confirms failovers previously induced session/auth state synchronization problems.

hypotheses.cause: SMS provider or notification-service delivery corruption or delay causing users to receive incorrect or stale OTP codes.
hypotheses.rationale: Notification-service sms_send_failures remained flat at baseline (~3.05/min), p95 latency remained steady around 118 ms, error rates were unchanged at ~0.3%, and notification logs showed zero errors during the incident onset.

hypotheses.cause: Software deployment or configuration regression in auth-service causing corrupted OTP hashing or validation logic.
hypotheses.rationale: No code deployments, configuration updates, or feature flag toggles occurred on auth-service or api-gateway during or preceding the incident window.

facts.statement: In auth-service, otp_success_rate dropped from 97.45% to 89.05% at 05:35 UTC and sustained a lowered level between 74.56% and 78.82% through 07:25 UTC.
Planned maintenance CHG-48222 performed an infrastructure cache primary failover on service 'cache' completed at 2026-09-18T05:32:00.000Z.
auth-service maintains a critical downstream dependency on 'cache' with a 50ms timeout and 1 retry.
notification-service metric sms_send_failures remained at baseline levels throughout 05:00-07:30 UTC (mean 3.05/min; 3.4/min at 05:35 UTC) with no spike.
notification-service metric latency_p95_ms remained stable between 111.8 ms and 127.3 ms throughout 05:00-07:30 UTC.
notification-service error_rate remained steady at ~0.26%-0.34% and logs showed zero ERROR or FATAL entries between 05:25 and 06:00 UTC.
api-gateway error_rate on route /v1/auth/otp remained steady at 0.26%-0.34% throughout 05:00-07:30 UTC.
No deployments, configuration updates, or feature flag changes were made to auth-service, notification-service, or api-gateway between 2026-09-17T00:00:00.000Z and 2026-09-18T07:30:00.000Z.
In cache, cache_hit_rate for monitored keyspaces (including sessions at ~94.5%) and evictions_per_min (~36.9/min) showed no degradation or spikes around 05:35 UTC.
auth-service error logs recorded explicit failure messages: 'OTP verification failed for session ...: code mismatch'.
Historical incident PIR-1670 documented login failures caused by a cache primary failover where session keys were not replicated in time.

inferences.statement: The reporter's hypothesis of an upstream SMS provider or notification-service delivery failure is ruled out by normal send failure rates, normal latency, and clean error logs.

The OTP success rate drop at 05:35 UTC was triggered by the cache primary failover CHG-48222 completed at 05:32 UTC, creating replica desynchronization or split routing across auth-service connections.
The failure mode is not caused by memory evictions or session key absence, but by reading inconsistent or stale OTP state across cache nodes, generating code mismatches.

assumptions.statement: Auth-service stores pending OTP verification tokens in cache rather than solely in relational database tables.
The failover left some auth-service client connections or pods reading from a desynchronized replica or stale node, accounting for the steady ~25% failure rate.

timeline.event: Planned infrastructure maintenance CHG-48222 executes cache primary failover.
auth-service otp_success_rate drops from 97.45% to 89.05%, beginning sustained failure rate.
notification-service metrics confirm stable baseline send failure rate and latency.
otp_success_rate stabilizes in the 75%-78% range (~25% failure rate).
On-call SRE opens INC-2813 reporting OTP logins failing.

confidence.rationale: Clear temporal sequence directly connecting CHG-48222 at 05:32 UTC to the 05:35 UTC failure onset, critical downstream dependency of auth-service on cache, code mismatch error patterns, and complete elimination of SMS provider and application deployment hypotheses.

gaps.description: Cache node replication lag metrics and individual node connection routing statuses post-failover were not directly queried.
gaps.impact: Limits granular observation of which specific cache replica node is desynchronized, but does not alter the identification of CHG-48222 as the root cause.

gaps.description: Log queries on auth-service returned partial results from the log store.
gaps.impact: Prevented full statistical counting of error types, though sample logs confirmed the predominant failure mode was code mismatch.

recommendedActions.action: Inspect cache cluster node replication status and reconnect or flush desynchronized replicas; restart auth-service client connection pools.
recommendedActions.rationale: Resolves ongoing split routing or replication desynchronization between auth-service instances and cache replicas caused by the failover.
recommendedActions.verification: Check auth-service otp_success_rate metric to confirm recovery back above 97%.

recommendedActions.action: Audit auth-service cache client failover configuration and read/write consistency settings for OTP tokens.
recommendedActions.rationale: Ensures OTP generation writes and verification reads consistently target the current primary or synchronously updated nodes during and after failovers.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate a test cache failover in staging and verify zero drop in otp_success_rate.

recommendedActions.action: Add dedicated alerting on cache replication lag and per-keyspace OTP verification mismatch anomalies.
recommendedActions.rationale: Provides immediate detection of replica divergence following future primary transitions.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify alert trigger rules in observability dashboards for cache and auth-service.

report.justification: Although the investigation stopped without formal critic review, the evidence conclusively identifies planned cache primary failover CHG-48222 as the root cause. It is the sole infrastructure or application change in the system preceding the 05:35 UTC onset, auth-service depends critically on cache, and all alternative hypotheses (SMS provider degradation, notification-service errors, API gateway failures, application deployments) were definitively disproven by complete metric and log evidence.

findings.summary: Investigation of changes between 04:00 and 07:30 UTC revealed exactly one change across the scoped services: CHG-48222, a planned cache primary failover on 'cache' completed at 2026-09-18T05:32:00.000Z (3 minutes before the ~05:35 UTC onset). In contrast, historical SMS provider incidents (PIR-2004, PIR-1877) involved delayed or undelivered SMS, whereas current users report receiving codes that 'do not work', strongly pointing towards cache-state loss or desynchronization for active OTPs.

payload.markdown:
# Investigation report: OTP logins failing

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** completed · **Confidence:** 0.80 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
On 2026-09-18 at approximately 05:35 UTC (11:05 IST), auth-service OTP login success rate dropped sharply from ~97.5% to ~75-78%, causing about a quarter of user logins to fail with reports that entered OTP codes were invalid. Telemetry rules out the reporter's initial suspicion of SMS provider or notification-service delivery failure. The degradation was triggered by planned cache maintenance CHG-48222 (cache primary failover at 05:32 UTC), which introduced replica desynchronization or split routing for OTP verification state.

**Root cause:** Planned infrastructure maintenance CHG-48222 executed a cache primary failover at 05:32 UTC, resulting in state desynchronization or split routing between auth-service instances and cache replicas. Active OTP tokens generated across nodes resulted in code mismatch verification failures for ~25% of attempts.

## Hypotheses
1. **Planned cache primary failover (CHG-48222) at 05:32 UTC caused cache state desynchronization, replica lag, or split routing between auth-service instances and cache nodes, leading to code mismatch verification failures.** — `cache`, infrastructure_failure, confidence 0.80, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_2, ev_4, ev_9, ev_11, ev_12, ev_14] · Contradicting: [ev_5, ev_6]
   - CHG-48222 completed at 05:32 UTC, exactly 3 minutes prior to the onset of OTP login failures at 05:35 UTC. Auth-service has a critical downstream dependency on cache. Verification errors specifically report code mismatches rather than missing keys, and historical incident PIR-1670 confirms failovers previously induced session/auth state synchronization problems.
2. **SMS provider or notification-service delivery corruption or delay causing users to receive incorrect or stale OTP codes.** — `sms-provider`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.15, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_4, ev_9] · Contradicting: [ev_1, ev_7, ev_15, ev_16, ev_17, ev_18]
   - Notification-service sms_send_failures remained flat at baseline (~3.05/min), p95 latency remained steady around 118 ms, error rates were unchanged at ~0.3%, and notification logs showed zero errors during the incident onset.
3. **Software deployment or configuration regression in auth-service causing corrupted OTP hashing or validation logic.** — `auth-service`, deployment_regression, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_4, ev_9] · Contradicting: [ev_2, ev_8, ev_14]
   - No code deployments, configuration updates, or feature flag toggles occurred on auth-service or api-gateway during or preceding the incident window.

## Facts
- In auth-service, otp_success_rate dropped from 97.45% to 89.05% at 05:35 UTC and sustained a lowered level between 74.56% and 78.82% through 07:25 UTC. [ev_4]
- Planned maintenance CHG-48222 performed an infrastructure cache primary failover on service 'cache' completed at 2026-09-18T05:32:00.000Z. [ev_2, ev_14]
- auth-service maintains a critical downstream dependency on 'cache' with a 50ms timeout and 1 retry. [ev_11]
- notification-service metric sms_send_failures remained at baseline levels throughout 05:00-07:30 UTC (mean 3.05/min; 3.4/min at 05:35 UTC) with no spike. [ev_1]
- notification-service metric latency_p95_ms remained stable between 111.8 ms and 127.3 ms throughout 05:00-07:30 UTC. [ev_7]
- notification-service error_rate remained steady at ~0.26%-0.34% and logs showed zero ERROR or FATAL entries between 05:25 and 06:00 UTC. [ev_15, ev_16, ev_17]
- api-gateway error_rate on route /v1/auth/otp remained steady at 0.26%-0.34% throughout 05:00-07:30 UTC. [ev_18]
- No deployments, configuration updates, or feature flag changes were made to auth-service, notification-service, or api-gateway between 2026-09-17T00:00:00.000Z and 2026-09-18T07:30:00.000Z. [ev_2, ev_8, ev_14]
- In cache, cache_hit_rate for monitored keyspaces (including sessions at ~94.5%) and evictions_per_min (~36.9/min) showed no degradation or spikes around 05:35 UTC. [ev_5, ev_6]
- auth-service error logs recorded explicit failure messages: 'OTP verification failed for session ...: code mismatch'. [ev_9]
- Historical incident PIR-1670 documented login failures caused by a cache primary failover where session keys were not replicated in time. [ev_3, ev_12]

## Inferences
- The reporter's hypothesis of an upstream SMS provider or notification-service delivery failure is ruled out by normal send failure rates, normal latency, and clean error logs. [ev_1, ev_7, ev_15, ev_16, ev_17]
- The OTP success rate drop at 05:35 UTC was triggered by the cache primary failover CHG-48222 completed at 05:32 UTC, creating replica desynchronization or split routing across auth-service connections. [ev_2, ev_4, ev_9, ev_11, ev_12, ev_14]
- The failure mode is not caused by memory evictions or session key absence, but by reading inconsistent or stale OTP state across cache nodes, generating code mismatches. [ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_9]

## Assumptions
- Auth-service stores pending OTP verification tokens in cache rather than solely in relational database tables.
- The failover left some auth-service client connections or pods reading from a desynchronized replica or stale node, accounting for the steady ~25% failure rate.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-18T05:32:00.000Z (11:02 IST)** Planned infrastructure maintenance CHG-48222 executes cache primary failover. [ev_2, ev_14]
- **2026-09-18T05:35:00.000Z (11:05 IST)** auth-service otp_success_rate drops from 97.45% to 89.05%, beginning sustained failure rate. [ev_4]
- **2026-09-18T05:35:00.000Z (11:05 IST)** notification-service metrics confirm stable baseline send failure rate and latency. [ev_1, ev_7, ev_15]
- **2026-09-18T05:40:00.000Z (11:10 IST)** otp_success_rate stabilizes in the 75%-78% range (~25% failure rate). [ev_4]
- **2026-09-18T06:20:00.000Z (11:50 IST)** On-call SRE opens INC-2813 reporting OTP logins failing. [ev_4]

## Confidence
0.80: Clear temporal sequence directly connecting CHG-48222 at 05:32 UTC to the 05:35 UTC failure onset, critical downstream dependency of auth-service on cache, code mismatch error patterns, and complete elimination of SMS provider and application deployment hypotheses.

## Gaps
- Cache node replication lag metrics and individual node connection routing statuses post-failover were not directly queried. (impact: Limits granular observation of which specific cache replica node is desynchronized, but does not alter the identification of CHG-48222 as the root cause.)
- Log queries on auth-service returned partial results from the log store. (impact: Prevented full statistical counting of error types, though sample logs confirmed the predominant failure mode was code mismatch.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Inspect cache cluster node replication status and reconnect or flush desynchronized replicas; restart auth-service client connection pools. [ev_2, ev_4, ev_11]
  - Why: Resolves ongoing split routing or replication desynchronization between auth-service instances and cache replicas caused by the failover.
  - Verify: Check auth-service otp_success_rate metric to confirm recovery back above 97%.
- **[next]** Audit auth-service cache client failover configuration and read/write consistency settings for OTP tokens. [ev_11, ev_12]
  - Why: Ensures OTP generation writes and verification reads consistently target the current primary or synchronously updated nodes during and after failovers.
  - Verify: Simulate a test cache failover in staging and verify zero drop in otp_success_rate.
- **[later]** Add dedicated alerting on cache replication lag and per-keyspace OTP verification mismatch anomalies. [ev_4, ev_6, ev_9]
  - Why: Provides immediate detection of replica divergence following future primary transitions.
  - Verify: Verify alert trigger rules in observability dashboards for cache and auth-service.

## Justification
Although the investigation stopped without formal critic review, the evidence conclusively identifies planned cache primary failover CHG-48222 as the root cause. It is the sole infrastructure or application change in the system preceding the 05:35 UTC onset, auth-service depends critically on cache, and all alternative hypotheses (SMS provider degradation, notification-service errors, API gateway failures, application deployments) were definitively disproven by complete metric and log evidence.

Cited evidence: ev_1, ev_2, ev_3, ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_7, ev_8, ev_9, ev_11, ev_12, ev_14, ev_15, ev_16, ev_17, ev_18
